open_findings.title: Concurrent refresh can return a new token on one request and tell another request to erase it.
Middleware timeout stops waiting but does not cancel database rotation or determine its eventual outcome.
Delivered 2FA proof can use a stale cached challenge after a newer challenge is committed.
Password-failure counters and lockout transitions are not atomic.
Reauthentication has no password-attempt throttle or durable failure budget.
Abuse-counter increment and initial expiration are separate cache commands.
Idempotency completion checks ownership and overwrites the reservation in separate commands.
Idempotency keys do not bind to request content.
Token refresh changes the session-management ID, invalidating a previously listed revoke target.
Temporary PostgreSQL failure is handled as permanent credential invalidation.
Synchronous lazy cache connection establishment falls outside the advertised async timeout.
PostgreSQL connection strings interpolate unescaped configuration values.
Public signup performs expensive password hashing before any signup abuse gate.
Default password-hash memory is passed in bytes, implying only 64 KiB.
Token replacement invalidates delivered tokens before delivery admission.
Unlock can clear a newer lockout using an earlier account/token snapshot.
Stale reset proof writes can replace a newer challenge or undo session revocation.
Removing the last additional factor allows a revoked reset session to be bypassed.
Password promotion does not atomically validate the completed reset proof session.
Reset creation and promotion acquire account/reset locks in opposite orders.
Expiration is not consistently enforced at the authoritative mutation point.
Concurrent duplicate signup returns a generic failure instead of the duplicate contract.
Concurrent verification resends can leave multiple usable verification tokens.
Infrastructure failure is reported and charged as missing/incorrect reset proof.
The fifth invalid bootstrap proof can reveal whether a reset request was real.
CAPTCHA configuration is disconnected from the actual request count and proof flow.
Reset cleanup exists but is not scheduled; reset events have no bounded retention.
Email/SMS factor enrollment trusts the active session without fresh sensitive-action proof.
Email/SMS verification can persist a factor after the account security stamp changes.
Default configuration ships a published TOTP encryption key that passes startup validation.
TOTP encryption has no key identifier or supported rotation path for existing enrollments.
Existing TOTP enrollments depend on mutable global algorithm, digits, and period settings.
Email/SMS verification and account-first factor mutations acquire locks in opposite orders.
Concurrent setup replacement can return success and deliver a code that was never persisted.
Setup delivery omits the account ID and bypasses the per-account delivery budget.
A TOTP enrollment lookup outage is charged as an invalid login proof.
Replacing pending authenticator setup with email/SMS retains abandoned TOTP secret material.
Recovery-email changes require no fresh password or existing-factor proof.
Final deletion can remove an account after its checked security stamp changes.
Pending deletion proofs survive account security-stamp and email changes.
Email completion and account deletion can deadlock through opposite lock order.
Failed-delivery cleanup erases the durable deletion-request cooldown and count.
Concurrent first deletion requests bypass the cooldown and overwrite the initial count.
Expired email-change reservations still block other accounts from requesting the address.
A concurrent address claim turns email completion into a generic server error.
Email verification GET performs the account change and session revocation immediately.
Activation verification can succeed twice or overwrite a concurrent cancellation/disable.
Disable never revokes an already verified activation.
Activation mutations can commit after the checked account security stamp changes.
Service expiration calculations disagree with the stored calendar term.
Delivery-denied creation still inserts retained activation rows without a request admission budget.
Activation delivery admission failures lose their reason and return generic HTTP 500.
All four activation repository methods commit with their reader still open.
